title: Grouped forearm muscle records from generate_artifact.py

muscles.name: Brachioradialis
muscles.origin: Upper 2/3 of lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus
muscles.insertion: Lateral base of styloid process of radius
muscles.primary_action: Primary elbow flexion in neutral/pronated forearm; stabilizes elbow during rapid movement
muscles.moment_arm: Elbow flexion moment arm: 5.0 - 7.5 cm (peaks at ~90-100 deg flexion). Dwarfs biceps moment arm in full pronation.

exercises.name: Reverse Barbell / EZ-Bar Curl
exercises.desc: Neutral/pronated grip eliminates biceps peak torque via radial tuberosity rotation; loads BR under heavy tensile mechanical tension (40-65 kg).

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.desc: Neutral alignment maximizes BR line of pull with joint-friendly mechanics.

exercises.name: Cable Cross-Body Hammer Curl
exercises.desc: Continuous resistance through entire elbow flexion arc.

muscles.mass_notes: Single largest individual muscle in the forearm (65.4 cm3). Located on the anterolateral margin of the proximal forearm, its hypertrophy directly creates the outer upper forearm 'sweep' and widens forearm diameter in both frontal and sagittal planes.

muscles.name: Flexor Digitorum Profundus (FDP)
muscles.origin: Upper 3/4 of anterior & medial ulna, interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Bases of distal phalanges of medial 4 digits (split through FDS tendons)
muscles.primary_action: Flexion of Distal Interphalangeal (DIP), PIP, MCP joints and wrist flexion
muscles.moment_arm: DIP/PIP flexion: ~0.8-1.0 cm; Wrist flexion: ~1.2-1.4 cm

exercises.name: Finger-Roll Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.desc: Allowing bar to roll to fingertips loads FDP under full active stretch across DIP joints before concentric wrist flexion.

exercises.name: Axle / Fat Grip Heavy Holds
exercises.desc: Massive isometric crush/support grip tension recruiting high-threshold motor units across large PCSA.

exercises.name: Arm Wrestling Hand Cup / Rolling Handle
exercises.desc: Dynamic flexion under severe load through full finger closure.

muscles.mass_notes: Highest PCSA in the entire forearm (14.5 cm2) and second largest volume (57.8 cm3). When combined with FDS, forms a 103.7 cm3 flexor engine (23.7% of total forearm mass). Dictates inner forearm depth and palm-to-forearm thickness.

muscles.name: Flexor Digitorum Superficialis (FDS)
muscles.origin: Humeroulnar head (medial epicondyle, coronoid) & Radial head (anterior oblique line)
muscles.insertion: Shafts of middle phalanges of medial 4 digits (slips split for FDP)
muscles.primary_action: Flexion of Proximal Interphalangeal (PIP) and Metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints, secondary wrist flexion
muscles.moment_arm: PIP/MCP flexion: ~1.1-1.3 cm; Wrist flexion: ~1.4 cm

exercises.name: Heavy Barbell Wrist Curls (Palms Up)
exercises.desc: Direct load through PIP flexion and wrist flexion moment arms.

exercises.name: Thick Bar / Towel Pull-Ups & Hangs
exercises.desc: Demands continuous high-force middle-phalanx isometric clamp.

exercises.name: Gripper Training / Hand Crush
exercises.desc: Progressive spring resistance through PIP closure arc.

muscles.mass_notes: Third largest individual muscle volume (45.9 cm3) and massive PCSA (10.8 cm2). Sits directly beneath the superficial flexor layer, pushing superficial muscles outward and expanding mid-forearm circumference.

muscles.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus (ECRL)
muscles.origin: Lower 1/3 of lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of base of 2nd metacarpal
muscles.primary_action: Wrist extension and radial deviation; assists weak elbow flexion
muscles.moment_arm: Wrist extension: ~1.5 cm; Radial deviation: ~1.8 cm; Elbow flexion: ~1.5-2.0 cm

exercises.name: Heavy Reverse Barbell Curl
exercises.desc: Acts as dynamic stabilizer holding wrist extended against gravity moment arm while assisting elbow flexion.

exercises.name: Rising / Radial Deviation with Strap/Lever
exercises.desc: Direct line of pull for radial abduction; dominant driver of wrist rising strength.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curls (Barbell/Cable)
exercises.desc: Direct concentric and eccentric wrist extension loading.

muscles.mass_notes: Large volume (38.2 cm3) located on the upper outer ridge right next to Brachioradialis. Together with ECRB, creates the upper posterolateral forearm 'shelf' that is instantly visible in short sleeves.

muscles.name: Flexor Carpi Ulnaris (FCU)
muscles.origin: Humeral head (medial epicondyle) & Ulnar head (olecranon & posterior ulna border)
muscles.insertion: Pisiform bone, hook of hamate, and base of 5th metacarpal
muscles.moment_arm: Wrist flexion: 1.8 cm (largest wrist flexion moment arm in human anatomy due to pisiform sesamoid elevation!); Ulnar deviation: 1.5 cm

exercises.name: Heavy Seated Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.desc: Takes maximum advantage of FCU's 1.8 cm moment arm and 7.9 cm2 PCSA to move 40-60 kg loads.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Back Standing Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.desc: Positions wrist in slight ulnar bias, isolating FCU under deep stretch.

exercises.name: Ulnar Deviation Lever / Arm Wrestling Cup
exercises.desc: Direct resistance against ulnar adduction torque.

muscles.mass_notes: Largest PCSA among all wrist-only flexors (7.9 cm2). Sits along the medial edge of the forearm; when flexed, forms the prominent medial muscle ridge from elbow to wrist.

muscles.name: Extensor Digitorum (ED / EDC)
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus via common extensor tendon
muscles.primary_action: Extension of MCP, PIP, DIP joints of digits 2-5; assists wrist extension
muscles.moment_arm: Finger extension: ~0.8-1.2 cm; Wrist extension: ~1.3 cm

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curls (Barbell / DB)
exercises.desc: Drives wrist extension and builds posterior dorsal bulk.

exercises.name: Wrist Roller (Extension Direction)
exercises.desc: High continuous time-under-tension across entire dorsal forearm.

exercises.name: Forearm Finisher / Resistance Band Finger Extensions
exercises.desc: Isolates digit extension to produce Roger C's 'piano strings' dorsal definition.

muscles.mass_notes: Covers the entire center of the posterior forearm (34.2 cm3). Hypertrophy of ED fills the flat dorsal aspect of the forearm, giving 3D roundness and visible striations upon extension.

muscles.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis (ECRB)
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus via common extensor tendon
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of base of 3rd metacarpal
muscles.primary_action: Primary wrist extension and weak radial deviation
muscles.moment_arm: Wrist extension: 1.6 cm (most direct central line of pull for pure wrist extension)

exercises.name: Reverse Barbell / Dumbbell Wrist Curl
exercises.desc: ECRB is the true prime mover of pure wrist extension, aligning directly through joint axis.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl Isometric Hold
exercises.desc: Maintains wrist in neutral against heavy flexion torque.

exercises.name: Rising Drills with Arm Wrestling Strap
exercises.desc: Co-contracts with ECRL to lock the wrist radially.

muscles.mass_notes: Sits deep and medial to ECRL. Combined with ECRL and BR, the Mobile Wad accounts for 136.4 cm3 (31.1% of total forearm mass). Essential for dorsal-lateral thickness.

muscles.name: Pronator Teres (PT)
muscles.origin: Humeral head (medial epicondyle) & Ulnar head (coronoid process)
muscles.insertion: Middle of lateral surface of radius (pronator tubercle)
muscles.moment_arm: Pronation moment arm: ~1.2-1.5 cm; Elbow flexion: ~1.0-1.4 cm

exercises.name: Judo Belt / Strap Pronation Drill
exercises.desc: As utilized by Roger C and arm wrestlers: wraps across back of hand, pulling into dynamic pronation against heavy resistance.

exercises.name: Off-Center Dumbbell / Hammer Pronation
exercises.desc: Pronating a sledgehammer or dumbbell loaded on one head creates maximal torque at horizontal.

exercises.name: Pronated Incline Reverse Curls
exercises.desc: Loads PT simultaneously as an elbow flexor and pronation stabilizer.

muscles.mass_notes: Forms the medial border of the cubital fossa in the proximal upper forearm (32.1 cm3, 6.8 cm2 PCSA). Hypertrophy of PT fills out the inner elbow pocket, making the upper arm and forearm merge seamlessly.

muscles.name: Flexor Carpi Radialis (FCR)
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus via common flexor tendon
muscles.moment_arm: Wrist flexion: 1.5 cm; Radial deviation: 1.0 cm

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl with Radial Tilt
exercises.desc: Curling with slight outward radial deviation directly follows FCR fiber line.

exercises.name: Standard Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.desc: Shares wrist flexion load with FCU and finger flexors.

exercises.name: Radial Deviation Rising Drills
exercises.desc: Co-contracts anteriorly to prevent wrist extension during rising.

muscles.mass_notes: Runs obliquely down the anterior radial side of the forearm (25.4 cm3). Its tendon is one of the most prominent landmarks on the palmar wrist.

muscles.name: Supinator
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus, supinator crest of ulna, radial collateral ligament
muscles.insertion: Proximal 1/3 of anterior and lateral surfaces of radius
muscles.primary_action: Pure forearm supination (unassisted by elbow position, unlike biceps brachii)

exercises.name: Offset Dumbbell / Sledgehammer Supination
exercises.desc: Resisting pronation torque with arm bent at 90 deg isolates the supinator.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Supination
exercises.desc: Roger C's prescribed antagonist drill to cure medial epicondylitis and restore arm wrestling balance.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Zottman Curl (Supinating Eccentric)
exercises.desc: Dynamic rotation through full supination arc under load.

muscles.mass_notes: Deep muscle wrapping tightly around the proximal radius (23.6 cm3). Crucial antagonist to Pronator Teres; neglecting it causes severe elbow torque imbalances and pain.

muscles.name: Extensor Carpi Ulnaris (ECU)
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle via common extensor tendon & posterior border of ulna
muscles.insertion: Medial side of base of 5th metacarpal
muscles.moment_arm: Wrist extension: ~1.2 cm; Ulnar deviation: ~1.6 cm

exercises.name: Ulnar Deviation Lever / Band Drills
exercises.desc: Essential antagonist drill mentioned by Roger C to balance high-volume rising/radial deviation.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curls with Ulnar Flare
exercises.desc: Emphasizes the ulnar posterior border.

exercises.name: Hammer Levering (Behind the Back)
exercises.desc: Loaded levering through ulnar deviation plane.

muscles.mass_notes: Forms the posterior ulnar margin of the forearm (20.3 cm3). Balances FCU on the ulnar border and prevents wrist instability.

muscles.name: Pronator Quadratus & Thumb Outcroppings (APL / EPB / EPL)
muscles.origin: PQ: Distal 1/4 anterior ulna; APL/EPB: Posterior radius/ulna/interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: PQ: Distal 1/4 anterior radius; APL: Base of 1st metacarpal; EPB/EPL: Proximal & distal phalanges of thumb
muscles.primary_action: PQ: Initiates pronation, binds radius & ulna; APL/EPB/EPL: Thumb abduction, extension, radial deviation
muscles.moment_arm: PQ pronation: ~1.0 cm; APL radial deviation: ~1.2 cm

exercises.name: High-Rep Rising Drills (Roger C Method)
exercises.desc: 5 sets of 60 reps with 10 kg strap loads APL, EPB and radial tendons continuously, stimulating collagen synthesis.

exercises.name: Heavy Plate Pinch Holds
exercises.desc: Demands maximum isometric thumb adduction and abduction stability.

exercises.name: Pronation Band Drills at Distal Wrist
exercises.desc: Forces PQ to resist distal radioulnar separation shear.

muscles.mass_notes: Pronator Quadratus is the ONLY true muscle belly situated in the distal 1/4 of the forearm. Hypertrophy of PQ combined with tendon sheath expansion accounts for the direct muscular component of wrist growth.
